memory_update.text: MECG.F should be tracked as the highest-purity underfollowed candidate for FC-BGA copper adhesion and surface-treatment chemistry, but later layers must confirm AI/HPC substrate revenue mix and customer linkage.
AJINY is a required reference leader for ABF insulating film, but its usefulness as an AI equity proxy is diluted by conglomerate exposure and needs segment materiality checks.
IBIDY is a reference substrate maker with official AI GPU and data-center MPU package-substrate exposure; later layers should test whether the market has already priced this node.
MKSI/Atotech belongs in the underfollowed adjacent lane as a US-listed package-substrate wet-chemistry, adhesion-promotion, plating, equipment, and process-control vendor.
US-primary listings are scarce for this node; most direct materials and substrate exposures are Japan/Taiwan/Korea companies accessible through OTC ADRs or foreign ordinary shares.
AJINY should be retained as the reference anchor for ABF insulating film, but group-level purity is a major underwriting issue because Ajinomoto is not a pure semiconductor materials company.

MECGF is the highest-priority underfollowed candidate for this node because copper-to-resin adhesion chemistry maps directly to FC-BGA substrate yield and has OTC US tradability, but liquidity and disclosure quality must be checked.
ESI is a plausible US-listed second-order chemistry candidate via MacDermid Alpha IC-substrate fabrication chemistry; it needs customer and revenue-mix verification before moving beyond Layer 1.

ONTO is a yield/process-control candidate rather than a materials supplier; include only if the research pass allows inspection, metrology, and defect analytics vendors tied to advanced IC substrates.

For this node, separate direct substrate-material chokepoints from HBM-stack tools: ABF insulating film and copper adhesion chemistry are exposed to accelerator package count and package complexity, not pure HBM bit growth.

Need a follow-up search for US OTC tickers and liquidity for Ibiden, Unimicron, Kinsus, AT&S, Shinko, and regional second-source ABF/adhesion chemistry candidates; they were not included here because the candidate list was capped at four.

US-listed pure-play exposure to Ajinomoto-like build-up insulating film or MEC-like copper-adhesion surface chemistry remains unconfirmed; Qnity is the closest US-listed materials candidate but must be tested for exact chemistry overlap.
Add Qnity Electronics (Q) to the AI FC-BGA substrate materials watchlist as a large-cap, newly spun-off electronics-materials reference name with explicit IC-substrate/FCBGA materials exposure.
Add Onto Innovation (ONTO) as a yield/process-control adjacency for advanced IC substrates and AI packaging, not as a direct material supplier.

Add Amtech Systems (ASYS) as a speculative micro-cap exception tied to AI semiconductor device packaging and advanced substrate fabrication equipment/consumables; require customer and FC-BGA process-step verification.

For this node, separate direct substrate-material suppliers from OSAT/package assemblers and from yield-inspection/equipment vendors; later layers should not treat all advanced-packaging exposure as direct FC-BGA chemistry exposure.
MKSI should be carried forward as the strongest US-listed underfollowed proxy for FC-BGA/package-substrate process chemistry via Atotech; verify AI/ABF/FC-BGA materiality in filings and calls.

CAMT should be carried forward as a mid-cap yield-inspection hypothesis for advanced packaging and possibly substrate-related inspection; survival requires evidence separating package-substrate exposure from general advanced-packaging/HBM inspection.

ONTO should be tracked as a larger-cap process-control and inspection candidate with AI advanced-packaging exposure, but its direct FC-BGA substrate-material linkage is weaker than MKSI and needs application-level confirmation.

For this node, US-listed names are mostly second-order process enablers rather than the dominant materials suppliers; the clean dominant suppliers cited in seed evidence are Ajinomoto for insulating film and MEC for copper adhesion chemistry.

Need a non-US-listed parallel map for Ajinomoto, MEC, Ibiden, Unimicron, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Nan Ya PCB, Shinko, and regional second-source chemistry/laminate suppliers before ranking the global chokepoint.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion found a narrow US-accessible universe for this node. The cleanest direct exposures are mostly non-US companies available through OTC ADR/foreign ordinary tickers rather than primary US exchange listings. Ajinomoto is the reference leader in ABF insulating film; MEC Company is the underfollowed purest copper-adhesion chemistry candidate; Ibiden is a reference substrate maker directly serving AI GPU/data-center package substrates; MKS Instruments/Atotech is a US-listed adjacent supplier of package-substrate wet chemistry, adhesion promotion, plating equipment, and process-control infrastructure. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded the US-tradable universe around the FC-BGA package-substrate materials and yield node. The strongest direct reference exposure is Ajinomoto via its OTC ADR because ABF is the dominant insulating film used in high-performance semiconductor package substrates. The strongest underfollowed chokepoint candidate is MEC Company via OTC ordinary shares because its copper-to-resin adhesion chemistry is directly tied to package-substrate yield. Element Solutions is a US-listed underfollowed second-source/adjacent chemistry candidate through MacDermid Alpha circuitry and IC-substrate process chemistries. Onto Innovation is included as a yield-enabling process-control vendor for advanced IC substrates and panel-level packaging rather than as a materials supplier. US-listed pure-play exposure to FC-BGA substrate insulating film and copper-adhesion chemistry appears scarce. The strongest direct chokepoint name
